events.lock is held for tens of seconds by short commands (ddflow update, heartbeat) under a many-agent fleet, so other writers time out after 30 s: ddflow update SEG-durations-record failed 3 times in a row, holders were 'ddflow update SEG-inflight-registry' and 'ddflow heartbeat'. The lock is held across work that need not be under it.

data.body: Follow-up of SEG-durations-record. Accept: (1) the unit_tests gate records junit durations into .ddflow/local/durations.json as ci does (reuse services/durations.capturing/stage_env); (2) the suite queue cost predictor (services/suitequeue.predicted_cost via suitelock, which has no repo handle today) falls back to the recorded file seconds when no run of its kind is measured; (3) ddflow metrics suitewaste reads the store. Test first for each. Falsifier: predicted cost differs from the measured median of the same kind by more than 2x on the replay of the last 50 runs. Size S.
data.title: Durations consumers: queue cost predictor, suitewaste and unit_tests read and record the store

data.body: Accept: after any ci run .ddflow/local/durations.json holds seconds per test id and per file (junit written by the run's pytest), the newest [suites].durations_keep runs kept, bounded by [suites].durations_max_mb; absent or unreadable junit records unavailable, not zero; [suites].record_durations switches it off. Test first: a fake runner emitting junit yields the file. Falsifier: recording adds more than 2 percent to wall time. Delivered here: the ci run. Moved to SEG-durations-consumers: the unit_tests gate recording, the queue cost predictor and ddflow metrics suitewaste reading the store. Size S.

data.claim: Folding a 22000-case junit into durations.json costs well under 2 percent of the measured 1656 s run (under 33 s)
data.falsifier: fold of 22000 cases takes over 33 s
data.mechanism: one parse and one atomic write of a ~1 MB json; pytest's junit writer adds a small per-test cost
data.probe: uv run python (record_junit of 22000 synthetic cases, twice)
data.probe_output: recorded 22000 tests/1300 files in 0.20 s, 0.18 s on a second run; file 1.24 MB (limit 8 MB)
data.question: Does recording per-test durations from junit cost under 2 percent of a full run?

evidence.note: claim CONFIRMED: fold of 22000 cases 0.20 s (limit 33 s); junit write cost inside pytest not measured here, only the fold

checked r-everything-configurable (3 knobs in [suites]), r-bounded-everything (keep N, max_mb, lock timeout), r-docs-with-the-change (help text withheld: parallel.md leased by another lane, to add), upgrade fragments added

chunk_findings.detail: Given a ci run with two test stages, stage A writes a valid junit report while stage B fails before writing its junit report or writes malformed XML. `stage_env` has already added B's report path to `cap.reports`, but `_fold_reports` suppresses B's read/parse error, sees cases from A, calls `record_cases`, writes `.ddflow/local/durations.json`, and returns `status: recorded`. The stated contract says an absent or unreadable junit report should record `unavailable` and leave the store untouched; here a run with a missing/unreadable stage report is recorded as successful with partial data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:_fold_reports

chunk_findings.detail: `load` only validates that `tests` and `files` are dicts, so a syntactically valid but corrupt store such as `{"schema":"durations@1","run":null,"tests":{},"files":{}}` is returned unchanged. `record_cases` then runs `int(data.get("run", 0))`, which raises `TypeError` for `None` (also for list/dict values). `record_junit` and `_fold_reports` catch only `OSError`, `ValueError`, `SyntaxError`, and `LockTimeout`, so the `TypeError` propagates and can abort the ci run or mask the original exception in `capturing`'s finally, contradicting the docstring that a bad file never blocks a run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:load/record_cases

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_ci_run_records_the_durations_of_its_command` constructs the command as `f"{shlex.quote(sys.executable)} {script}"`, but `script` is interpolated unquoted. If the temporary repository path contains spaces (for example `pytest --basetemp="/tmp/my tests"`, or a Windows `%TEMP%` path under `C:\Users\Name With Space\...`), the command becomes something like `python /tmp/my tests/repo_fake_pytest.py`. When `CI.run` executes that command as a shell command or via `shlex.split`, it will try to run `/tmp/my` or pass wrong arguments, so the fake pytest never writes the junit report and the test fails even though duration recording is working. The script path needs to be quoted as well.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_durations_record.py:181

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_ci_run_with_recording_off_adds_nothing_to_the_environment` runs `test -z "$PYTEST_ADDOPTS"` without clearing the ambient `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` value. If the developer or CI environment already exports a non-empty `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (e.g. `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-q pytest tests/test_durations_record.py`), the shell expansion makes `test -z` fail, so `res.status` is not `"passed"` and the test fails even though `record_durations=False` correctly added no value. The test needs to delete/neutralize the variable (e.g. `monkeypatch.delenv("PYTEST_ADDOPTS", raising=False)`) or otherwise test that the run did not modify it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_durations_record.py:191

chunk_findings.detail: `record_report` catches only `OSError` around `Path(report).read_text()` and does not check `cfg.suites.record_durations` before reading. If the junit file exists but is not valid UTF-8, `read_text()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is a `ValueError`, so the function propagates the exception instead of returning `{"status": "unavailable", ...}`. If `record_durations` is false, the same input still causes the read and can raise, so the off switch does not prevent a corrupted report from breaking the caller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:record_report

chunk_findings.detail: `load` only validates that the top-level `tests` and `files` values are dicts; it does not sanitize corrupt rows or an invalid `run`, despite the docstring promising that a bad store never blocks a run. For example, if `.ddflow/local/durations.json` is `{"schema":"durations@1","run":null,"tests":{},"files":{}}`, a valid junit report reaches `record_cases`, where `int(data.get("run", 0))` raises `TypeError`. `record_junit` and `_fold_reports` catch only `OSError`, `ValueError`, `SyntaxError`, and `fsio.LockTimeout`, so the exception escapes and the ci run fails instead of treating the store as empty/unavailable. A non-dict test row similarly causes an uncaught `AttributeError` in `_fold_in`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:load/_fold_in

chunk_findings.detail: The capturing path treats a partially missing or unreadable report set as a successful record. If `stage_env` creates two report paths, the first is written with test times, and the second is missing or unreadable, `_fold_reports` suppresses the second report's error, sees cases from the first, calls `record_cases`, and returns `{"status": "recorded", ...}` after writing the store. The module docstring says a missing or unreadable report records `unavailable` and leaves the store untouched; here the missing stage's durations are silently absent while the run is reported as recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:_fold_reports

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_ci_run_with_recording_off_adds_nothing_to_the_environment` asserts that the CI command sees an empty `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` by running `test -z "$PYTEST_ADDOPTS"`. If the pytest process is started with `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` set, e.g. `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-q pytest tests/test_durations_record.py`, that variable is inherited by the CI command unless the runner explicitly scrubs it. With recording disabled, the correct behavior is “do not add anything,” not “clear any pre-existing value,” so an inherited non-empty `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` makes the command fail and the test fail even though recording is off. The test should unset/ignore the ambient variable or compare the runner environment before and after enabling recording.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_durations_record.py:188-194

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_ci_run_records_the_durations_of_its_command` builds the CI command as `f"{shlex.quote(sys.executable)} {script}"`, leaving the script path unquoted. If the temporary repo path contains spaces, the shell or command splitter splits the script path into multiple arguments, so `CI.run` executes the wrong command and the test fails. The executable is quoted, but the script path should be quoted too.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_durations_record.py:182

chunk_findings.detail:
`_clean_rows` excludes booleans from the duration samples but not from the row counter/timestamp `at`: `at if isinstance(at, int) else 0` is true for `True`/`False` because `bool` subclasses `int`. Given a corrupt store row such as `{"s": [1.0], "at": true}`, `load` returns that row with `"at": True` instead of dropping it or coercing it to an integer counter. This preserves a malformed value in the store and can be serialized back as JSON `true`, contrary to the function’s stated rule that only well-formed rows survive.

Previous findings 3 and 4 are in `tests/test_durations_record.py`, which is not included in this part; they cannot be verified from the supplied delta.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/durations.py:_clean_rows
